shape: Step by step down from scale step 6 to step 1, above a held tonic note
parameters: Notes B-flat A G F E D. Upbeat. Dotted rhythm on beats 2 and 4. Low register

shape: A semitone down, then a leap of a tritone
parameters: Intervals -1, then 6. It is the start of themes 2b, 4a, and 5a

shape: Two semitone steps a fourth apart
parameters: Example: the semitone above step 5 and the semitone below step 1

shape: A unit of 1 bar, said two times at the same pitch, then a longer continuation
parameters: Proportion 1 : 1 : 2. The second statement is not on the dominant

shape: The first theme of a group starts low. The range goes up as the section continues
parameters: Themes 1a; 2a; 3a start in the low register

shape: Each new theme is a changed form of an earlier theme: same contour, new intervals or new rhythm
parameters: Rhythm of the upbeat: present (1a); empty (2a; 4a); present again (5a)

shape: The same theme with a new character
parameters: Same contour; intervals adjusted; arpeggio inverted

shape: The last motive of a phrase starts the next phrase
parameters: The new phrase starts before the cadence is complete

shape: Three earlier themes at the same time in the tonic major
parameters: Themes 1a, 7a, and 10

item: Diatonic theme with a chromatic inner voice
shape: A melody that goes up by diatonic steps, with an inner voice that goes down by semitones
parameters: Contrary motion

item: Fugue subject in a narrow range
shape: Four phrases. Each phrase fills a block of adjacent semitones. The line goes up to the centre and back
parameters: Range A to E-flat in the first statement; all semitones from A to E in the subject

shape: The same theme later with larger intervals: chromatic steps become diatonic steps
parameters: Example: I bars 1-5 and IV bars 204-209
where: Music for Strings I and IV

shape: After the climax, the subject is always inverted. At the end, the subject and its inversion sound together
parameters: Both lines start on A and end on A

shape: Short motive at an irregular time in the bar
parameters: Six different imitations: birds, cicadas, frog. Bartók: the player can put them at any point and play as many as he likes

item: Repeated note that becomes a melody
shape: Repeated notes that start as noise and change into the shepherd's melody
parameters: The note G-sharp, from bar 37

shape: A A A C A A: five notes in the time of four, then one more
parameters: Latent rhythm 3 + 2 + 1. It sounds like an acceleration that stops suddenly

shape: One line, no accompaniment, sometimes doubled one or two octaves apart
parameters: Pentatonic (G A C D F), old Hungarian style

shape: A melody "shown" as a sound of the place, not as the voice of the composer
parameters: Strict Dorian mode on C-sharp

shape: The calls of real birds that the composer wrote down
parameters: Tufted titmouse and wood thrush, heard in North Carolina in 1945

shape: A theme of rising fourths in the low strings
parameters: Cellos and basses; answered by string tremolo and flutes

shape: A short part of a real folk song as the main motive
parameters: Three notes: E F-sharp G

shape: One note repeated in even values, and a chain of minor thirds that are not adjacent
parameters: The thirds go up in the Prelude and down in the Fugue

shape: One repeated note with ornaments
parameters: The note C, played by oboes "in a highly primitive manner"

shape: A known piece of music that comes from far away
parameters: Offstage piano: the Albéniz-Godowsky Tango. Hymn: Rock of Ages. Bach chorale

shape: Short sentences about friends, set as melodies for solo instruments. Then the words are removed
parameters: Melodies above the chaconne chords

item: All material from the first solo
shape: The full movement comes from the first solo passage
parameters: Also the chord that functions as the tonic

shape: Many solo players echo the calls of the others
parameters: Calls made from repeated notes and minor thirds
